Show HN: Harness Relay – the coding agents you have, working together
items.summary: If you already have multiple coding agents(one kind of agent also works though), you should really look into this project! It's a desktop app that brings coding agents working together, with user experience similar to ChatGPT! One kind of agent is enough for an agent team: all of one kind, or any mix of Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Cursor Agent, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot CLI, Muse Code and five open-source coding agents on your own model backends. For each question, the lead agent designs the team: each member’s role and model, and how they take turns. Once you confirm it, the real agents on your machine work on your code, or any question, and answer each other. It also supports voice input, notification, branching in conversation, task scheduling, and mobile app(PWA) support! If you are interested in this project, please give it a try and star us on the GitHub repo, thanks! GitHub repo: https://github.com/Agentic-System-Lab/harness-relay

items.title: Show HN: Port of Context – Token efficient MCP context layer
items.summary: Hi HN, I'm working on a context layer built on OSS and open standards that lets agents search your company knowledge and use MCP tools all through a single gateway with code mode. Building this because we believe context can and should be portable across harnesses. The metric we are solving for here is "cost to resolution". Given any question or a task, how quickly and cheaply can we put an agent on the correct path. Tech behind that: 1. Context map: software to create and maintain a context map of people, teams, systems, relationships, etc. It's built on OKF, import/export from this open standard. 2. Code mode: agents explore the map with a token efficient context eng. method (open source runtime, find portofcontext/pctx on GitHub) 3. Indexing: Hybrid keyword and semantic search on any unstructured text, with code mode on top (we will open source this part soon, although it's nothing special, the interesting part is placing content in the map and putting code mode on it) Some proof that it works: 1. Goose + code mode: https://aaif.io/blog/how-port-of-context-eliminated-producti... 2. tau-bench: https://portofcontext.com/blog/context-layer-platform-benchm... With Port of Context To try it, paste this into your coding agent: Set up pctx.ai/onboard.md It will help you create an account, scan your active MCP connections, and help configure the gateway. Hope you find this useful and feel free to reach out: patrick@portofcontext.com
